reviews.title: Trapped in an onboarding nightmare
reviews.text: This is the most ADHD unfriendly app ever created. The registration process feels like a interrogation. You can't even skip questions that don't apply to you. It creates so much mental noise and clutter before you even start. If I wanted to feel trapped, anxious and bored out of my mind, I’d go to DMV, not download a " helpful" app. Deleted in 5 minutes.

reviews.title: Want to use but it’s completely pay app
reviews.text: This would be a good game changer if it had a free option without a trial

reviews.title: Fun & Very Informative
reviews.text: It’s a cool app i definitely learned a few things ! I wish it was totally free to use so I cannot continue using it but I liked it for the short time I got to use it either way !!

reviews.title: No refunds
reviews.text: I've tried to cancel this app a couple of times and they continue to charge me annually. They just charged me $199.00 yesterday and I can't get a refund.

reviews.title: Great App
reviews.text: This is the first and only app that I have stuck with and that actually helps. The lessons are short and to the point makes it super easy to digest and implement. I am really surprised and impressed given that I have been attempting to find something that works for me for literally years. Having insurance and taking advantage of the therapist match is amazing. I love my therapist and I have never been able to find someone that I feel comfortable with. I recommend for any adult that has had this life long struggle. I also have never written and review - that is how impressed I am!!!
Too damn expensive

reviews.title: It’s Me - All of it, it’s Me!
reviews.text: It’s astonishing to me, answering a few questions led to a personalized vision of myself. I can’t wait to find myself again, life is spiraling. Love the explanation, insight and direction to stop the vicious cycles! I cannot wait to share this navigational tool with my children. Thank you Inflow, where have you been my entire life!

reviews.title: Widget
reviews.text: I’m just starting with the app after a recent burnout situation. One thing that would really help is a widget for daily check in. ADHD is such a see it or forget it issue that a widget vs just another app icon would help me remember to do my check ins and keep it front of mind.

reviews.title: Re-training My Brain  - Old Dog, New Tricks
reviews.text: I found out just last year that I have, (and have had all my life), ADHD.  Since then, with more research on symptoms and overall awareness of psycho-pathology, I believe that I also have some autistic and OCD traits.  I have found the exercises in this app to be not only useful but helpful in understanding and working with instead of against myself.  I look forward to the rest of the sessions.  Thank you, Inflow.

reviews.title: TRULY changed my life
reviews.text: I don’t think we realize how much of our problems are rooted in ADHD. These modules truly helped heal my mental health by better understanding my brain. It teaches you helpful strategies and also teaches you to have more compassion for yourself the more you learn about your brain.

reviews.title: My favorite app

reviews.title: So much here!!
reviews.text: Very comprehensive!  There are spaces in the app for different kinds of learning and reflection from quick 4 min. Lessons to 40 min webinars to peruse.  There are spaces for open ended musings and very pointed comprehension quizzes.  Take it all or parts of it when time allows.  I’ve already learned so much in one week.

reviews.title: Insightful & educational
reviews.text: The presentations & exercises have given me great insight into behaviors I can work on & have helped me accept myself.

reviews.title: Too Expensive
reviews.text: I’m giving this one star for the fact that this app is outrageously expensive! The developer has made it out of reach…not many people can afford nearly $50 per month for an app. Would be nice if you could come up with a cheaper option for people who aren’t able to afford it.

reviews.title: I deleted this app within hours of starting the free trial.
reviews.text:
I use unique email addresses and phone numbers for every service I sign up for so I can identify when my information is shared or misused. Less than four hours after creating my Inflow account, I received a text message on the phone number that I had only ever used for Papa John’s. While I can’t say with certainty how it happened, the timing was concerning enough that I no longer trusted the service with my data.

What made things worse was trying to delete my account. Instead of providing a straightforward in-app process, I was directed to a Notion page to request deletion of my data. It felt unprofessional, was unnecessarily difficult to navigate, and didn’t inspire confidence that a company handling sensitive personal information takes privacy seriously.

Based on my experience, I won’t be using this app again.

reviews.title: “Free trial” scam
reviews.text: I have no idea how I signed up for a three month free trial. I didn’t have any sign up emails or even a log in/password but just randomly got charged $200. I’m assuming it’s my own error but also that this app has dark UX. A sneaky free trial for ppl with ADHD that they have to remember to cancel and don’t even remember signing up for is predatory imo

reviews.title: Predatory Scam
reviews.text: Avoid this app at all costs.  They have double charged me and many other users.  They do not answer any queries through their email.  They advertise a very accommodating refund policy which seems to be a scam. After my trial I cancelled my subscription but was charged twice. Despite multiple attempts to contact them at the only available email address on their site, they have not replied after two months.  There are better options available that do not prey on users. I am shocked this app is still allowed on the App Store.

reviews.title: Admitting it’s real

reviews.title: Second Best Time is Now
reviews.text: I’m late diagnosed with AuDHD and before I found out, I was gathering all these science-backed resources together to create a system in Notion. This tool centralizes and simplifies many of those concepts and adds practice and quiz elements to it so the habits stick better. My favorite part is the measuring progress over time in areas that I struggle with. I wish I had found this app sooner, but second best time is now!

reviews.title: So so
reviews.text: It’s not bad. I have learned a few things along the journey so far and I think knowledge is half of the battle. Especially if you just found out you have ADHD. Some of the tools are not as useful. I paid for the Quinn AI and I think it is probably helpful if you use it to work through things. I have found that I don’t use it very often. I paid for the archetype test and while it is spot on in some areas there are others that are completely inaccurate. There is no way to take the test again which kind of sucks. The other community based tools are interesting but it doesn’t have an open section where you could throw out something you’re struggling with and have the community respond. Overall, I like it but I don’t know that I’ll renew once the subscription comes back around.

reviews.title: Stupid
reviews.text: As someone with ADHD… these modules are not great for the money you pay. There’s barely on here and it sucks not worth it… seriously

reviews.title: Predatory billing and exploits ADHD symptoms
reviews.text:
I signed up for a free 7 day trial in May 2024. The app will redirect you to enter payment information on their website so the billing date will not show under your app store subscriptions. If you cancel before the end of the trial period you immediately lose access to the app. Inflow also does not send an email when they bill you. I have paid $600 for an app that I used for less than a week over 2 years ago. Inflow takes advantage of people diagnosed with ADHD because we are more likely to struggle with forgetfulness and staying organized. 

Even if you do remember to use the app, it contains tips that you will see on any other ADHD app or blog and the layout of the app is not engaging. 

Living with ADHD has made me feel like I am inferior to my peers many times in my life and getting duped by this app certainly did not help.

reviews.title: Voiceover Issues
reviews.text: I'd like to try this app out, but I can't get beyond the account creation screen with voiceover. ONCE this app has it's accessibility issues fixed, I'll be happy to come back and give it a higher rating.

reviews.title: Paywall
reviews.text: I signed up out of curiosity for help managing my ADHD. After a lengthy registration process, they herded me into a free trail. It pops up and doesn’t allow you to X out the screen. You either have to subscribe or exit the app. I didn’t even know if I’d like using the app, much less want to take a free trial before I could even look at how everything is laid out. I contact support to have my account deleted. Waste of time.

reviews.title: Module Frustration
reviews.text: I absolutely love the Coworking & Focus Rooms on Inflow and the community built in both of them. I love learning so much about ADHD in the modules too. However, I miss the way the modules used to be, when you clicked “View All” you could really see ALL the topics. Now you can only “View All” of the categories of modules like “Organization” or “Family” but not all of the topics are listed under these categories. I’ve taken to just typing in random letters in the search bar just to find the other hidden topics.

reviews.title: A lonely girl who never knew ADHD could be why
reviews.text: I took the adhd test just playing around. But answered the questions honestly. Imagine how surprised I was when it told me I was 95% matched with the ADHD diagnosis. After this first day and talking to my AI Quinn it’s all making sense how I look at things and respond is affecting my whole life! I have to learn how not to do those things and this app is going to help they really focus it around what you need to improve on and what you need to work on!

reviews.title: Finally
reviews.text: This app was recommended by Coby Watts and I adore and trust him so I went for it and could not be happier with the small bite-sized nuggets of wisdom and encouragement. And that I don’t have to do more than a minute at a time to succeed on here!

reviews.title: Love yourself as you are no matter how hard it is to accept that in your brain ❤️
reviews.text: Really enjoyed this module, especially the last one on self acceptance

reviews.title: So far, life changing.
reviews.text: I’m only on day 1 of my trial so I’m sure things will change, but so far I am loving this app and what it’s teaching me. I love Quinn (the AI chatbot) for the personalized help on top of learning from each (short) module. My only critique thus far is to maybe consider adding a widget that I can add to my homescreen to remind me to check in each day.

reviews.title: Recently diagnosed
reviews.text: I seen inflow on instagram and thought it would be one of those where you answer all the questions then it makes you pay to get the results and i have been pleasantly surprised no payment required to get your results and since downloading Inflow I have felt so seen and it makes me feel so happy to know that they understand and I’m not alone. My favorite part about this app has been when it said “ you have a free trial and if you forget to cancel let us know within 7 days and we will refund you” I am soo forgetful that this meant sooo much to me bc they know the struggle. I will continue to use inflow. Thank you🫶🏽🥲

reviews.title: Starting out
reviews.text: So if you are about this change then this is a great assist. The AI assistant is great and I’m liking how it keeps me going by not overwhelming me with info.

reviews.title: Pretty accurate so far…
reviews.text: I’m on the free trial period but so far like what I see. The content is short, bitesize and structured. Easily digestible.

reviews.title: 2nd try
reviews.text: This is the second time I’ve tried to use this app and I find it simply not useful. I have paid $240 to learn the pomodoro technique and how to start the smallest part of a project. I don’t know if the app just doesn’t work for my brand of adhd or it’s just as basic as the flyer I was given with my diagnosis but I’m done giving them money.

reviews.title: Get this
reviews.text: Omg this app helped my overthinking more than dbt or my outpatient program. If you have trouble with self compassion. This app makes it understandable and it’s interactive enough to practice. It also does bite size pieces daily which helps my adhd brain

reviews.title: Not for Me
reviews.text: There is sooo much reading. For someone who has difficulty focusing and reading, there are just too many words on the screen. Also as someone with misophonia, the narrator’s voice drives me crazy. I lasted 10min on this app. 😩
